prompt: Quick audit a mixed Python pytest target: one unit test starts asyncio.create_task and asserts before joining it, one unit test cancels and awaits a task while asserting the cancellation outcome, one ASGI integration test uses a client without entering the app lifespan or closing its session, and one integration test enters lifespan and verifies the resource is closed. Preserve the project's documented runner, existing fake-clock or sleep policy, fixtures, and cleanup conventions.
expected_artifacts: loaded Python core and unit/integration addons
required_checks: load references/extensions/python/core.md and the selected Python unit/integration addons
classify the detached task as python.HC-7
classify the observed cancellation as python.POS-6
classify the lifespan or teardown bypass as python.I-HC-A3
classify startup plus observable shutdown as python.I-POS-4
preserve the project's documented runner and existing clock/sleep, fixture, and cleanup rules
forbidden_behaviors: treat asyncio.create_task or an ASGI client as a smell by name alone
replace the project's runner with pytest or prescribe a new clock/sleep policy
duplicate generic fixture or filesystem cleanup findings
design the Python service or audit its TLS/SSRF controls
grader: rubric: Python unit and integration routing distinguishes detached async work from observed lifecycle evidence, cites only the four new Python codes where their contracts are visible, and keeps sibling ownership and project conventions intact
ip_handling: original synthetic prompt; no third-party text

prompt: Quick audit a token-validation unit test that asserts the wrong error message. The test covers a public authentication entry point.
required_checks: derive risk tier as high for the auth path per materiality signal
emit warn severity with the high SUT risk tier so the finding would rank P0 on a Deep remediation worklist (do not fabricate a worklist in quick mode)
cite the materiality grounding in the risk-tier field
forbidden_behaviors: assign medium or low risk tier without a grounding signal
report P1 for a warn finding on a high-risk-tier path
grader: rubric: output derives high risk tier from the auth-path signal and maps warn × high to P0 per audit-craft.md §3 priority table
ip_handling: original synthetic prompt; no third-party text

prompt: Quick audit an integration test that calls a payment confirmation endpoint but only asserts the HTTP 200 status code. Emit a finding with all five C fields.
required_checks: emit a Consequence field naming what ships undetected if this finding is not remedied
cite a smell code as criteria
pair the Consequence field with severity
forbidden_behaviors: omit the Consequence field from the finding
replace Consequence with a generic summary
emit a bare opinion without a cited smell code
grader: rubric: output carries all five C fields and the Consequence field names the downstream effect if the control weakness ships per audit-craft.md §3
ip_handling: original synthetic prompt; no third-party text

prompt: Quick audit a mixed Node and React target: one unit test starts a promise, timer, worker, and node:test subtest but observes none; one observes a promise result and clears its timer; one component test rerenders after an Effect request but lets stale data replace the current view; one rerenders and asserts stale completion cannot change the visible view; one integration test starts a server and pool but never observes close; one drives readiness, serves a request, closes its owner, and verifies the resource was released. Preserve the documented runner and existing cleanup conventions.
expected_artifacts: loaded Node core and unit/integration addons
required_checks: load references/extensions/nodejs/core.md and the selected Node unit/integration addons
classify detached work as nodejs.HC-8 only when its outcome is unobserved
classify observed completion or cleanup as nodejs.POS-8
classify missing React Effect cleanup or stale-work proof as nodejs.HC-U2
classify observable Effect cleanup or stale-work protection as nodejs.POS-U2
classify missing lifecycle-owner evidence as nodejs.I-HC-A4
classify observable lifecycle ownership as nodejs.I-POS-4
preserve the documented runner and existing cleanup conventions
forbidden_behaviors: treat promise, timer, worker, subtest, server, pool, or useEffect API-name presence alone as a smell
replace the project's runner or cleanup policy
design application cancellation architecture
audit TLS, SSRF, or worker-message security controls
grader: rubric: Node and React routing distinguishes unobserved detached work from observable outcomes, Effect cleanup from API-name findings, and integration lifecycle ownership from incidental close calls while preserving sibling boundaries
ip_handling: original synthetic prompt; no third-party text
